summary: Transformer models of viral protein evolution (DASM, in PyTorch), joint models of deep mutational scans ([multidms](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/#multidms), in JAX), neural-network global epistasis models (torchdms, in PyTorch), and recurrent networks for recombination-rate estimation ([ReLERNN](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/#relernn), in TensorFlow/Keras).
Pulling biological signal out of noisy experiments: regularized and sparse models, global epistasis, Bayesian methods, and simulation to generate training data and validate methods.
Python for nearly everything; C++ for tree-sequence recording in the SLiM simulator; R, Bash, and JavaScript where a project called for them.
Wrangling and encoding large biological datasets, from phylogenies of 13M+ viral genomes to multidimensional PhIP-Seq data.
Figures for papers in *Cell* and *eLife*, and interactive tools such as [phippery](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/#phippery)'s Streamlit app and multidms's interactive plots.

Reproducible pipelines in Nextflow and Snakemake (one ran 50K+ jobs on an HPC cluster), containers with Docker and Apptainer, CI with GitHub Actions, and sensitive-data management on HPC file systems and AWS S3.
